title_en: Chen Shundi v. Zhejiang Lexue'er Household Products Co., Ltd., He Jianhua, and Third Party Wen Shidan — dispute over infringement of invention patent
ruling_gist_en: The key to determining whether the step sequence of a method patent limits the scope of protection of the patent right, thereby restricting the application of the doctrine of equivalents in step interchange, is to assess whether these steps must be performed in a specific order and whether such interchange would result in substantial differences in technical functions or technical effects.

full_text_en:
Chen Shundi v. Zhejiang Lexueer Household Products Co., Ltd., He Jianhua, and Third Party

Wen Shidan — dispute over infringement of invention patent

Ruling Summary

I. In examining whether the order of steps in a process patent limits the scope of patent protection, thereby restricting the application of the doctrine of equivalents in the context of step swapping, the key is to determine whether those steps must be performed in a specific order and whether such swapping results in substantive differences in technical function or technical effect.

II. The application of Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases shall be determined as of the date of the alleged infringing act.

III. Where an alleged infringer commissions a third party to manufacture products in accordance with samples provided by the alleged infringer, such act shall be deemed as an act of implementation by the alleged infringer.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2013) Min Ti Zi No. 225

Re-Petitioner (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Zhejiang Lexueer Household Products Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. XX, Houjie Village, Hongjia Street, Jiaojiang District, Taizhou City, Zhejiang Province.

Legal Representative: Zhou Wenping, Executive Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Yang Ying, lawyer of Liaoning Tongze Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Chen Shundi, male, Han ethnicity, born on June 14, 1962, residing in Taizhou City, Zhejiang Province.

Agent ad litem: Dong Shibo, lawyer of Zhejiang Kaiwang Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance: He Jianhua, male, Han ethnicity, born on March 14, 1964, residing in Shenyang City, Liaoning Province.

Third Party at First Instance: Wen Shidan, male, Han ethnicity, born on October 28, 1967, residing in Xingcheng City, Liaoning Province.

Re-Petitioner Zhejiang Lexueer Household Products Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lexueer Company) filed a petition for retrial with this Court, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2011) Liao Min San Zhong Zi No. 27 rendered by the Liaoning High People's Court (hereinafter "the High Court"), in the dispute with Respondent Chen Shundi, Defendant at First Instance and Appellant at Second Instance He Jianhua, and Third Party Wen Shidan over infringement of invention patent. This Court issued a civil ruling (2013) Min Shen Zi No. 720 on September 29, 2013, granting the retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on November 29, 2013. Yang Ying, agent ad litem for Lexueer Company, and Dong Shibo, agent ad litem for Chen Shundi, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. He Jianhua and Wen Shidan, having been duly summoned by this Court, did not appear in court. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

On September 17, 2010, Chen Shundi filed a lawsuit with the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province (hereinafter "the Court of First Instance") on the grounds that the cloth-plastic hot water bottles produced and sold by Lexueer Company, and sold and offered for sale by He Jianhua, infringed his invention patent for "Processing Method of Cloth-Plastic Hot Water Bottle." The claims sought were: 1. An order that He Jianhua immediately cease selling infringing products, and Lexueer Company immediately cease manufacturing and selling infringing products, and destroy the infringing products and molds; 2. An order that He Jianhua pay Chen Shundi RMB 500,000 in economic damages, and Lexueer Company pay Chen Shundi RMB 1,000,000 in economic damages (including reasonable expenses incurred by Chen Shundi in stopping the infringement); 3. An order that Lexueer Company and He Jianhua bear the litigation costs of this case.

The Court of First Instance found the following facts upon trial: On February 24, 2006, Chen Shundi filed an application with the State Intellectual Property Office for an invention patent titled "Processing Method of Cloth-Plastic Hot Water Bottle." The patent was granted on February 17, 2010, with patent number 200610049700.5, and the patent remains valid to date. The patent claims are as follows:

1. A processing method for a cloth-plastic hot water bottle, wherein the cloth-plastic hot water bottle comprises a bottle body, a bottle mouth, and a bottle stopper; the bottle body has an inner layer, an outer layer, and an insulating layer; the edges of the bottle body have bonding edges; the bottle stopper comprises a threaded seat and a threaded cap; the outer wall of the threaded seat has a composite layer; the threaded cap has a sealing gasket; the threaded seat of the bottle stopper is made of polypropylene material, the composite layer is made of polyvinyl chloride material, and the sealing gasket is made of silicone material; characterized in that:
Step 1: First, take the inner layer, insulating layer, and outer layer materials;
Step 2: Second, sequentially laminate the inner layer, insulating layer, and outer layer to form a combined layer;
Step 3: Third, overlap two combined layers correspondingly, and use a high-frequency heat sealing machine to perform high-frequency heat bonding on the edges of the two combined layers according to the shape of the hot water bottle;
Step 4: Fourth, cut the high-frequency heat-bonded hot water bottle into individual pieces;
Step 5: Fifth, injection-mold the threaded seat from polypropylene material, then place the threaded seat as an insert into a mold, and additionally injection-mold a composite layer of polyvinyl chloride material around the threaded seat;
Step 6: Sixth, install the threaded seat with the composite layer into the bottle mouth, so that it contacts the inner layer, and use a high-frequency heat sealing machine to heat-bond the mouth portion of the hot water bottle to the composite layer of the threaded seat;
Step 7: Seventh, trim the edges of the hot water bottle body;
Step 8: Eighth, injection-mold the threaded cap from plastic material;
Step 9: Ninth, injection-mold the sealing gasket from silicone material;
Step 10: Tenth, assemble the sealing gasket and the threaded cap together, then screw them into the threaded seat;
Step 11: Eleventh, perform air inflation pressure testing, inflating the hot water bottle with compressed air for pressure resistance testing;
Step 12: Twelfth, package.
(For convenience of expression, the above steps are referred to by their corresponding Arabic numerals below.)

On September 7, 2010, under the supervision of notaries from Liaoning Provincial Chengxin Notary Public Office, Zhang Yong, agent ad litem for Chen Shundi, acting as an ordinary consumer, purchased 40 "Lexueer" brand fashionable hot water bottles (one large-size and 39 medium-size) on the fourth floor of Shenyang Small Commodity World, located at No. 17, Dongshuncheng Street, Dadong District, Shenyang. He obtained an invoice titled "Liaoning Province Shenyang Small-Scale Paste-in Invoice" stamped with the seals of "Shenyang Dadong District Ren Guoliang Grocery Wholesale Department General Invoice Special Seal" and "Shenyang Dadong District Ren Guoliang Grocery Wholesale Department, Shenyang Small Commodity World Market Stall 4044," and a business card of a salesperson from that store bearing the words "Stall 4107, 4044, Fourth Floor, Shenyang Small Commodity World, Ren Guoliang." The invoice recorded the unit price of the large-size hot water bottle as RMB 15 and the unit price of the medium-size hot water bottle as RMB 5. The notaries photographed the hot water bottles obtained through the purchase and sealed one large-size bottle and two medium-size bottles. The outer packaging bags of the hot water bottles obtained through notarization bore the "Lexueer" trademark and information such as "Taizhou Lexueer Plastic & Electrical Co., Ltd."

Between November 17, 2009, and November 3, 2010, agents ad litem for Chen Shundi conducted notarizations of purchases of cloth-plastic hot water bottles manufactured by Lexueer Company in Taizhou City, Zhejiang Province; Yantai City, Shandong Province; Weifang City, Shandong Province; and Wuhan City, Hubei Province, among other locations. On September 29, 2010, under the supervision of notaries, Chen Shundi notarized the process of logging onto the website at www.tzlxe.cn. The homepage of that website prominently displayed "Zhejiang Lexueer Household Products Co., Ltd." and under "Latest Supply" showed "Supply of Cloth-Plastic Hot Water Bottles" with accompanying photographs of the products. The "Company Introduction" section of the website stated "Annual Turnover: RMB 20 million/year to RMB 30 million/year."

On September 28, 2010, upon Chen Shundi's application, the Court of First Instance conducted evidence preservation at Lexueer Company concerning the inventory quantity, processing method, and sales ledgers of the alleged infringing products. Lexueer Company presented to the Court of First Instance 21 boxes of cloth-plastic hot water bottle products from its warehouse but refused to allow the court to preserve evidence of its processing method and sales ledgers. During the trial at first instance, Lexueer Company confirmed that all preserved samples were manufactured and sold by it and that all samples were made according to the "Hot Water Bottle Process Description" submitted to the court. Lexueer Company stated that steps 1-4 and step 11 of the alleged infringing method were identical to steps 1-4 and step 12 of Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit; steps 6, 7, 8, and 10 of the alleged infringing method corresponded respectively to steps 7, 6, 11, and 10 of Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit; and the alleged infringing method did not include steps 5, 8, and 9 of Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit. Lexueer Company refused to provide evidence regarding its sales ledgers.

It was further found that He Jianhua was the operator of the Shenyang Dadong District Ren Guoliang Grocery Wholesale Department, located at Stall 4044 in the Shenyang Small Commodity World Market. The third party, Wen Shidan, was the operator of the Shenyang Dadong District Yonglilai Grocery Wholesale Department, located at Stall 4107 in the Shenyang Small Commodity World Market. Ren Guoliang was a salesperson for both Stall 4044 and Stall 4107. Lexueer Company was formerly known as Taizhou Lexueer Plastic & Electrical Co., Ltd., which changed its corporate name to Lexueer Company on March 23, 2010.

The Court of First Instance held: 1. On the issue of whether Lexueer Company had infringed Chen Shundi's patent-in-suit. Lexueer Company argued that the insulating layer in the patent claim was a functional description, while in the alleged infringing method, what was placed between the inner and outer layers was half-piece hollow thin cotton, which did not possess the technical features of an insulating layer. The Court of First Instance held that the patent claim did not limit the material or size of the insulating layer, and therefore did not support Lexueer Company's above defense. Lexueer Company admitted that the first four steps and the last step of the alleged infringing method were identical to the first four steps and the last step of Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit, and the Court of First Instance confirmed this. Lexueer Company argued that steps 6, 7, 8, and 10 of the alleged infringing method corresponded respectively to steps 7, 6, 11, and 10 of Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit, but in a different order, and thus did not fall within the scope of protection of the patent. The Court of First Instance held that for these four steps, whether performed in the order of the alleged infringing method or in the order of the patent claim, there was no substantive difference in technical features or technical effects, and therefore did not support Lexueer Company's above defense. Lexueer Company argued that the alleged infringing method did not include steps 5, 8, and 9 of Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit. Upon review, steps 5, 8, and 9 of Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit were respectively the processing methods for the threaded seat, the threaded cap, and the sealing gasket. The structure and material of the corresponding three components of the alleged infringing product were identical to those of the product directly obtained by the patented method. Although Lexueer Company claimed that the product components corresponding to these three parts were purchased externally, regarding the details of the purchase, Lexueer Company stated that it provided the samples, and the supplier produced according to the material and structure of the samples, delivering according to the order quantity. Lexueer Company refused to explain or provide evidence regarding the source of the samples and the supplier's production process. The Court of First Instance held that the purchase and sale contract submitted by Lexueer Company was signed after the alleged infringing products had left the factory, and Lexueer Company failed to prove its authenticity and performance. Lexueer Company also failed to explain or provide evidence regarding the processing method of the three components. Therefore, the court did not support Lexueer Company's defense that the alleged infringing method lacked steps 5, 8, and 9 of Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit. Lexueer Company argued that the alleged infringing method originated from the specific embodiment disclosed in the specification of utility model patent No. ZL200520015446.8, and thus constituted prior art. However, Lexueer Company failed to prove that the technical features of the alleged infringing method were identical or had no substantive differences from the corresponding technical features of the utility model patent. Therefore, the court did not support its prior art defense. In summary, the technical features of the alleged infringing method fully covered all the essential technical features of the patent claim. Lexueer Company, knowing that Chen Shundi owned the patent-in-suit, still used the patented method for production and sold the products directly obtained by the patented method, thereby infringing the patent-in-suit and should bear the legal liability of ceasing infringement and compensating for losses. 2. On the issue of whether He Jianhua had infringed the patent-in-suit. He Jianhua was the operator of Stall 4044 and should bear legal liability for the acts of his salesperson Ren Guoliang in purchasing and selling the alleged infringing products. Because He Jianhua failed to provide evidence of the legitimate source of the alleged infringing products, he could not be exempted from liability for damages. Chen Shundi's claim that He Jianhua had engaged in offering for sale the alleged infringing products was not supported by evidence, and the Court of First Instance did not uphold it. 3. On the issue of the amount of damages. Since Chen Shundi did not provide evidence of his actual losses or the specific amount of profits gained by the infringer from the infringement, the Court of First Instance, taking into comprehensive consideration factors such as the type of the patent-in-suit, the nature, circumstances, scope, and duration of the infringement, and the reasonableness of the actual expenses incurred by Chen Shundi in investigating and stopping the infringement, determined the amount of damages in this case ex officio and discretionarily.

In summary, on December 17, 2010, the Court of First Instance rendered civil judgment (2010) Shen Zhong Min Si Chu Zi No. 389, ordering: 1. He Jianhua shall immediately cease selling the alleged infringing products upon the judgment taking effect; 2. He Jianhua shall, within ten days after the judgment taking effect, pay Chen Shundi RMB 10,000 in economic losses and reasonable expenses; 3. Lexueer Company shall immediately cease the infringing acts upon the judgment taking effect; 4. Lexueer Company shall, within ten days after the judgment taking effect, pay Chen Shundi RMB 300,000 in economic losses and reasonable expenses; 5. Chen Shundi's other claims were dismissed.

Both Lexueer Company and He Jianhua, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Liaoning High People's Court (hereinafter "the Court of Second Instance").

Upon trial, the Court of Second Instance found the following facts: The Court of First Instance's finding that Lexueer Company admitted that steps 1 and 2 of the alleged infringing method were identical to steps 1 and 2 of the patent claim was incorrect; otherwise, the other facts found by the Court of First Instance were true, and the Court of Second Instance confirmed them. It was further found that on April 28, 2010, Lexueer Company entered into a "Purchase and Sale Contract" with a third party, Ren Jinyan, agreeing that Lexueer Company would purchase from Ren Jinyan 20,000 sets of hot water bottle caps (including gaskets) and 20,000 sets of hot water bottle threaded seats, which were to be delivered together; 3,000 sets (1,500 each of large and small) were to be delivered before May 10, 2010, and the balance was to be settled before August 30, 2010. This contract had been fully performed. It was further found that on September 7, 2010, the stall at which Zhang Yong, agent ad litem for Chen Shundi, purchased the "Lexueer" brand hot water bottles on the fourth floor of Shenyang Small Commodity World was Stall 4107. During the proceedings of the Court of Second Instance, Chen Shundi applied to withdraw his claims against He Jianhua.

The Court of Second Instance held that it was inappropriate for the Court of First Instance to require Lexueer Company to bear the burden of proof regarding the processing method of the three components: the threaded seat, the threaded cap, and the gasket. Lexueer Company admitted that the threaded seat in the alleged infringing product was injection-molded from polypropylene material, and its composite layer (polyvinyl chloride material) was formed on the surface of the threaded seat by injection molding; the threaded cap and gasket were injection-molded from plastic material and silicone material, respectively. Therefore, the processing methods of these three components were the same as steps 5, 8, and 9 of Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit. Even if these components were manufactured by another processor based on samples provided by Lexueer Company, Lexueer Company should bear legal liability for such processing act. Therefore, the Court of Second Instance did not support Lexueer Company's appeal argument that the alleged infringing method lacked steps 5, 8, and 9 of Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit. Although steps 6 and 7 and steps 8 and 10 of the alleged infringing method were in a different order from steps 6 and 7 and steps 10 and 11 of Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit, their technical features and technical effects had no substantive differences. The patent claim did not limit the material or size of the insulating layer, and the hollow cotton in the alleged infringing method served a certain insulation function, equivalent to the insulating layer in Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit. Therefore, the Court of Second Instance did not support Lexueer Company's appeal arguments that the order of steps 6 and 7 and steps 10 and 11 was reversed and that the alleged infringing method lacked the insulating layer described in Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit. The evidence provided by Lexueer Company to prove that the alleged infringing method was prior art only disclosed some technical features of the alleged infringing method, and the alleged infringing method was equivalent to the patent-in-suit. Therefore, Lexueer Company's prior art defense could not stand. In conclusion, the technical features of the alleged infringing method fully covered all the essential technical features of the patent-in-suit, and Lexueer Company's acts infringed the patent-in-suit. The amount claimed by Chen Shundi for compensation from Lexueer Company included royalties for the period of provisional patent protection and damages for infringement. Chen Shundi did not provide evidence to prove the amount of his losses or the profits gained by Lexueer Company from the infringement. The Court of First Instance's determination that Lexueer Company should compensate Chen Shundi RMB 300,000 in economic losses and reasonable expenses, based on factors such as the type of patent, the nature, circumstances, scope, and duration of Lexueer Company's infringement, and the reasonableness of the actual expenses incurred by Chen Shundi in investigating and stopping the infringement, was not improper. In summary, the Court of Second Instance rendered judgment: 1. Affirming items 3, 4, and 5 of the first-instance judgment; 2. Reversing items 1 and 2 of the first-instance judgment. Court costs of first instance in the amount of RMB 18,300 were to be borne by Chen Shundi in the amount of RMB 14,500 and by Lexueer Company in the amount of RMB 3,800; court costs of second instance in the amount of RMB 5,850 were to be borne by Lexueer Company in the amount of RMB 5,800 and by Chen Shundi in the amount of RMB 50.

Lexue'er Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of the second instance, applied to this Court for retrial, arguing: (1) The alleged infringing method did not fall within the scope of protection of Claim 1 of the patent in suit and thus did not constitute infringement. 1. The alleged infringing method did not include steps 5, 8, and 9 of Claim 1 of the patent in suit, namely, the steps of processing the threaded plug seat, threaded plug cap, and sealing gasket. The three above-mentioned components in the hot water bottles produced by Lexue'er Company were all legally purchased from external sources, and the processing method for the externally purchased components was injection molding. Lexue'er Company had no obligation to know the processing method of the samples. The courts of first and second instance erred in ruling that Lexue'er Company bore the burden of proof for the processing method of the above three components and further presumed that Lexue'er Company had adopted the same method as the patent in suit. 2. The order of steps 6 and 7 and steps 10 and 11 of the alleged infringing method was reversed compared to that of Claim 1 of the patent in suit, and this change in step order produced different technical effects. The change in steps 6 and 7 could save space occupied by the processed product in the subsequent processing step, improve processing efficiency, and allow the product to directly enter the inspection step. The change in steps 10 and 11 eliminated the need to install the plug cap before removing it for inflation testing, saving time and ensuring test quality. Since the patent in suit claims a product processing method, both the steps themselves and the order between steps in a method claim should limit the scope of protection of the patent right. Moreover, the specification of the patent in suit recorded an order of steps interchanging steps 10 and 11. According to the doctrine of dedication, this alternative step order recorded in the specification should not be included within the scope of protection of the patent in suit. Therefore, the change in steps in the alleged infringing method did not fall within the scope of protection of the patent in suit. 3. The hollow cotton soft pad in the alleged infringing product was not an identical or equivalent technical feature to the thermal insulation layer recorded in the patent in suit. The court of first instance improperly expanded the scope of protection of this functional limitation technical feature. Based on the description of the thermal insulation layer in the specification of the patent in suit and the content disclosed in the drawings, the thermal insulation layer is located between the outer layer and the inner layer, with its four edges completely connected to the outer and inner layers, fully covering and isolating the outer and inner layers, so as to achieve improved thermal insulation performance, slow heat dissipation and cooling, extended use, and overcoming the initial scalding phenomenon when hot water is poured in. The purpose of the thin hollow cotton soft pad provided between the outer and inner layers of the alleged infringing product is to increase the comfort of holding the hot water bottle. It is only provided in the middle part of the outer and inner layers, with a certain distance from the upper and lower edges to the outer and inner layers, and does not fully cover and isolate the outer and inner layers as in the patent in suit. Therefore, it cannot have the technical effect produced by the thermal insulation layer of the patent in suit. (2) The product and process method contained in the patent licensed to Lexue'er Company constitute prior art, and Lexue'er Company's use of this method to produce and sell the alleged infringing product does not constitute infringement. The filing date of Utility Model Patent No. ZL200520015446.8 was October 10, 2005, which is earlier than the filing date of the patent in suit. The product disclosed in this prior art is the same as the product recorded in the claims of the patent in suit, and it explicitly discloses steps 3, 5, and 6 of Claim 1 of the patent in suit. Since cloth-plastic and PVC hot water bottles are conventional types of hot water bottles, the other steps not explicitly disclosed, namely steps 1, 2, 4, and 7-12, all belong to common general knowledge and customary means. In particular, the inflation test in step 11 is an industry standard for hot water bottle products. (3) Chen Shundi did not claim compensation for the royalties for the period of provisional protection in the first instance. The original judgment of the second instance, which determined a compensation amount of RMB 300,000 including such royalties, exceeded Chen Shundi's claims. Furthermore, the grant date of the patent in suit was February 17, 2010, and Chen Shundi filed the present lawsuit in September 2010. Since most of the period from February to September is the off-season for hot water bottle sales, and sales volumes were very small, the court of first instance's award of RMB 300,000 in damages to Lexue'er Company was excessive. In summary, Lexue'er Company requested this Court to revoke the judgments of the first and second instances, amend them to dismiss Chen Shundi's claims, or remand the case for retrial.

Chen Shundi argued: 1. Whether the order of steps in a method invention limits the claims should be determined in conjunction with the description and drawings. If the description and drawings explicitly state that the technical effect claimed by the invention can be achieved without following the order of steps, or if a person of ordinary skill in the art can deduce, based on common general knowledge, that the technical effect claimed by the invention can be achieved even if the order is not followed or certain steps are not followed in order, then the order of steps in the method invention does not constitute a limitation on the claims. The content recorded in the specification of the patent in suit, indicating that the order of steps 10 and 11 can be interchanged, shows that these two steps do not need to be performed in a strict order. The numbering of the step order in the claims of the patent in suit is merely for simplicity and clarity of description. The doctrine of dedication applies only to technical solutions described only in the specification but not recorded in the claims. In this case, Claim 1 does not exclude the technical solution described in the specification, so the doctrine of dedication does not apply to this case. The order of steps 6 and 7 and steps 10 and 11 in Claim 1 of the patent in suit does not limit Claim 1; moreover, applying the doctrine of equivalents, there is no substantial difference between the technical features after interchanging steps 6 and 7 and steps 10 and 11 in the patent in suit and those before the interchange, constituting equivalent infringement. 2. The purchase and sale contract submitted by Lexue'er Company was signed after the alleged infringing product left the factory, and Lexue'er Company failed to prove its authenticity and performance. Lexue'er Company did not explain or provide evidence for the processing method of the three components involved in steps 5, 8, and 9 of Claim 1 of the patent in suit. Furthermore, even if these components came from a third party, Lexue'er Company's use of them for further manufacturing and subsequent use and sale of the infringing product also constitutes infringement. 3. The hollow cotton soft pad of the alleged infringing product has the thermal insulation effect described in the patent in suit and is an equivalent technical feature to the thermal insulation layer of the patent in suit. 4. The utility model patent relied upon by Lexue'er Company for the prior art defense discloses a product, whereas the patent in suit is a method invention. Therefore, unless the specification of the utility model patent explicitly records the specific manufacturing steps of the product, or a person of ordinary skill in the art can unambiguously deduce the specific manufacturing steps, the manufacturing process of a product cannot be deduced from its structure alone. In analyzing the manufacturing steps of the utility model patent product, Lexue'er Company used a large number of personal deductions and guesses not supported by other evidence. 5. Chen Shundi claimed compensation for the royalties for the period of provisional protection in the first instance. The determination of such compensation in the judgment of the second instance did not exceed Chen Shundi's claims, and the amount of compensation was reasonable. In summary, Chen Shundi requested this Court to dismiss Lexue'er Company's retrial request.

Facts found by the Court: The facts found in the judgments of the first and second instances are basically accurate. Additionally, page 2 of the specification of the patent in suit records: "The bag body of this hot water bottle is composed of three layers of material. Because of the thermal insulation layer, the heat in the bag decreases slowly, avoiding overheating at the beginning, providing long-lasting heat preservation, and improving the use effect." In the specific implementation part on that page, it records: "A thermal insulation layer 5, such as artificial thermal insulation cotton and other relevant materials, is installed between the inner layer 4 and the outer layer 3, improving the thermal insulation performance of the hot water bottle, allowing slow heat dissipation and cooling, extending the use time, and overcoming the initial scalding phenomenon when hot water is poured in." Page 3 records: "Step Ten: Assemble the sealing gasket 10 and the threaded plug cap 9 together and then screw them into the threaded plug seat 8; but it is also possible to screw in the plug cap after pressure testing. Step Eleven: Inflation pressure test, inflate the hot water bottle with compressed air for a pressure test; the pressure for the pressure test is generally 0.5 kg/cm, or slightly higher."

Lexue'er Company admitted that the materials of the threaded plug seat, threaded plug cap, and gasket in the alleged infringing product were the same as those of the corresponding components in the patent in suit and were also formed by injection molding; although the threaded plug seat was formed by two-stage molding, the processing method was different from that of the patent in suit, where the two-stage injection molding was performed on two machines, whereas now the vast majority are completed on a single machine. The utility model patent specification No. ZL200520015446.8 for "a new type of hot water bottle" submitted by Lexue'er Company recorded that the grant and announcement date of the patent was December 27, 2006.

The Court considers: The disputed issues in this case are whether Lexue'er Company's prior art defense is established; whether the processing method of the alleged infringing product falls within the scope of protection of the patent in suit; whether the determination of compensation for the royalties for the period of provisional protection in the original judgment of the second instance exceeded Chen Shundi's claims; and whether the determination of the amount of compensation in the original judgments of the first and second instances was manifestly unfair.

I. Whether Lexue'er Company's prior art defense is established

Article 62 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law) provides: "In a patent infringement dispute, if the alleged infringer has evidence to prove that the technology or design implemented by it belongs to the prior art or prior design, it does not constitute infringement of the patent right." Article 22, paragraph 5, of the Patent Law provides: "'Prior art' as used in this Law means technology that was known to the public domestically and abroad before the filing date of the patent." Although the filing date of Utility Model Patent No. ZL200520015446.8 relied upon by Lexue'er Company for the prior art defense is earlier than the filing date of the patent in suit, its grant and announcement date is later than the filing date of the patent in suit. Therefore, it does not constitute prior art but constitutes a conflicting application according to law. Since a conflicting application can destroy the novelty of the technical solution of the compared patent, when the alleged infringer argues that it does not constitute patent infringement by implementing the technical solution in the conflicting application, it should be allowed, and the review criteria for the prior art defense may be referred to for evaluation. Utility Model Patent No. ZL200520015446.8 is a product patent for "a new type of hot water bottle." From its claims, specification, and drawings, this patent only discloses a hot water bottle product and does not disclose the specific production steps of this hot water bottle product. Although some steps in the hot water bottle processing are conventional steps, only a general processing flow can be determined based on the product disclosed in the patent, and the specific complete processing steps cannot be accurately determined. Moreover, the patent does not disclose technical features such as the material composition of the plug seat and the presence of a sealing gasket at the plug cap. Although Lexue'er Company argued that the undisclosed technical features were common general knowledge and customary means in the art, it did not provide evidence to prove this. Therefore, Utility Model Patent No. ZL200520015446.8 does not fully disclose the processing method of the alleged infringing product. Lexue'er Company's prior art defense based on this patent cannot be established, and this Court does not support it.

II. Whether the processing method of the alleged infringing product falls within the scope of protection of the patent in suit

The disputes between Lexue'er Company and Chen Shundi regarding the alleged infringing method and the method of the patent in suit mainly focus on step 5, 8, and 9, steps 6 and 7, steps 10 and 11, and the thermal insulation layer technical feature in Claim 1.

1. Regarding the dispute over steps 5, 8, and 9. Lexue'er Company argued that the threaded plug seat, threaded plug cap, and gasket of the alleged infringing product were all ordered and purchased from third parties based on samples provided by Lexue'er Company. Lexue'er Company had no obligation to bear the burden of proof for the processing method of the externally purchased components, and the alleged infringing method lacked steps 5, 8, and 9 of Claim 1 of the patent in suit. This Court holds that Lexue'er Company admitted that the material and structure of the externally purchased components were the same as those of the components directly obtained through the processing method of steps 5, 8, and 9 of Claim 1 of the patent in suit, and admitted that the processing process of the externally purchased components was injection molding, and that the threaded plug seat was also formed by two-stage injection molding. Thus, it can be determined that the processing method of the above components is the same as that of steps 5, 8, and 9 of Claim 1 of the patent in suit. Although Lexue'er Company argued that the vast majority of threaded plug seats were completed on a single machine, which was different from the processing method of the patent in suit, step 5 of Claim 1 of the patent in suit does not limit the specific processing method of two-stage injection molding. Whether the two-stage injection molding is completed on a single machine does not constitute a limitation condition for this step. Therefore, Lexue'er Company's above argument cannot be established. Accordingly, the key to this dispute turns to whether Lexue'er Company implemented steps 5, 8, and 9, i.e., whether the alleged infringing method lacks steps 5, 8, and 9. This Court holds that, according to Lexue'er Company's statement, although the above components were not processed by itself, they were custom-made by a third party based on samples provided by Lexue'er Company. That is, these components were processed and produced by the third party according to Lexue'er Company's requirements. Therefore, Lexue'er Company shall bear the corresponding legal liability for the legal consequences arising therefrom. Consequently, Lexue'er Company's argument that the alleged infringing method lacks steps 5, 8, and 9 has no factual or legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

2. Regarding whether the interchange of steps constitutes equivalent infringement. Claims of method invention patents include activities with a time process, such as manufacturing methods, use methods, communication methods, and processing methods. Invention patents involving product manufacturing methods are usually realized through the combination of method steps and a certain step order. The key to determining whether the step order of a method patent limits the scope of protection of the patent right, thereby restricting the application of the doctrine of equivalents in step interchange, is whether these steps must be implemented in a specific order and whether such interchange leads to substantive differences in technical function or technical effect. Specifically in this case, step 6 of Claim 1 of the patent in suit is the step of thermally bonding the mouth portion of the hot water bottle and the composite layer of the threaded plug seat; step 7 is the step of trimming the bag body of the hot water bottle. The steps adopted in the alleged infringing method are to first trim the bag body of the hot water bottle, and then thermally bond the mouth portion of the hot water bottle and the composite layer of the threaded plug seat. Lexue'er Company argued that following this step order could save space occupied by the processed product in subsequent steps, facilitate rapid processing and improve processing accuracy, and allow the product to directly enter the inspection step. This Court holds that, from the previous processing steps of the alleged infringing method, the hot water bottle had already been cut after high-frequency thermal bonding in step 4. At this point, the main purpose of trimming is to make the hot water bottle look better and closer to the finished product. Its space-saving effect is very limited, and the existence of excess scraps does not interfere with the bonding of the plug seat and has no substantive impact on the bonding of the plug seat. Therefore, the implementation of these two steps does not have a unique one-to-one correspondence in order. Whether trimming is performed first or thermal bonding is performed first has no substantive impact on the realization of the entire technical solution. Moreover, the interchange of these two steps does not produce substantive differences in technical function or technical effect. Therefore, the interchanged steps in the alleged infringing method are equivalent technical features to steps 6 and 7 of Claim 1 of the patent in suit.

Step 10 of Claim 1 of the patent in suit is to assemble the sealing gasket and the threaded plug cap together and then screw them into the threaded plug seat; step 11 is the inflation pressure test. The alleged infringing method adopts the steps of first performing the inflation pressure test, and then assembling the sealing gasket and the threaded plug cap together and screwing them into the threaded plug seat. Lexue'er Company argued that the effect brought by this step interchange is that it is not necessary to remove the threaded plug cap after installing the threaded plug seat for inflation testing, thus saving time and ensuring test quality. This Court holds that the inflation pressure test of the hot water bottle needs to be performed through the mouth portion of the hot water bottle. According to the operation of steps 10 and 11 of Claim 1 of the patent in suit, before performing the inflation pressure test, the threaded plug cap must be unscrewed from the threaded plug seat. Compared with the steps adopted in the alleged infringing method of performing the pressure test first and then assembling the threaded plug cap, this operation step essentially adds an operation link for the inflation pressure test, resulting in extended operation time and reduced efficiency. Therefore, after interchanging the order of steps 10 and 11, the technical effect of reducing operation links, saving time, and improving efficiency as argued by Lexue'er Company is indeed produced. Therefore, the differences in technical effects produced by this step interchange are substantive, and the interchanged steps are not equivalent technical features to steps 10 and 11 of Claim 1 of the patent in suit.

Chen Shundi argued that the specification of the patent in suit has already recorded that the order of steps 10 and 11 can be interchanged, and Claim 1 does not exclude the technical solution described in the specification. Therefore, the technical solution with interchanged steps should be included within the scope of protection of the patent in suit, and the doctrine of dedication should not apply to this case. This Court holds that accurately determining the scope of protection of a patent right is not only necessary to provide effective legal protection for the patentee, but also to respect the notice and boundary-drawing function of the claims and to safeguard the reliance interests of the public. The establishment of the doctrine of dedication in claim construction is the result of balancing the protection function and the notice function of a patent. The meaning of this rule is that technical solutions described in the patent specification but not reflected in the claims cannot be included within the scope of protection of the claims. For technical solutions disclosed in the specification but not recorded in the claims, if the doctrine of dedication is not applied, although the protection for the patentee may be more adequate, on the one hand, this would provide convenience for patent applicants to circumvent examination of broader claims, and on the other hand, it would reduce the boundary-drawing effect of the claims, making the determination of the scope of protection of the patent right overly flexible and uncertain, increasing the difficulty for the public to predict the scope of protection of the patent right, and being detrimental to the play of the notice function of the patent and the maintenance of public interests. Therefore, Article 5 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Infringement of Patent Rights stipulates: "Where the patentee, in a dispute over patent infringement, includes a technical solution that is only described in the specification or drawings but not recorded in the claims within the scope of protection of the patent right, the people's court shall not support it." This judicial interpretation came into effect on January 1, 2010. The alleged infringing act in this case occurred in September 2010, so the above provisions of this interpretation can apply to this case. According to the provisions of the above article, if a person of ordinary skill in the art, upon reading the specification, can understand that a technical solution disclosed but not claimed is specifically identified as another option for the technical features in the claims, then such technical solution is deemed to be dedicated to the public. This is precisely the situation in this case. The specification of the patent in suit explicitly records on page 3 that the order of steps 10 and 11 can be interchanged, but this interchanged step is not reflected in the claims. Therefore, the interchanged steps cannot be included within the scope of protection of the patent in suit. Lexue'er Company's argument that the doctrine of dedication should apply to the step interchange solution of steps 10 and 11 is legally based, and this Court supports it.

3. The issue of whether the "hollow cotton soft pad" and the "insulation layer" constitute equivalents. According to the description of claim 1 of the patent in dispute, the insulation layer is a technical feature defined by function. Article 4 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases provides: "For a technical feature expressed in terms of a function or effect in a claim, the people's court shall, in light of the specific embodiments of such function or effect described in the specification and drawings and their equivalent embodiments, determine the content of such technical feature." The hot water bottle produced according to the patented method in dispute has a total of three layers, namely an inner layer, an outer layer, and an insulation layer. According to the description of the insulation layer in the specification of the patent in dispute and the content disclosed in the drawings, the insulation layer is made of various relevant materials such as artificial insulation cotton, located between the inner layer and the outer layer, completely covering and isolating the inner layer and the outer layer, and can achieve the following technical effects: improving insulation performance, slowly dissipating heat and cooling down, extending usage time; overcoming the phenomenon of being too hot at the beginning when hot water is poured. The hollow cotton soft pad in the accused infringing product has a width equal to that of the inner layer and the outer layer, and is connected to the left and right side edges of the inner layer and the outer layer; its length is equivalent to half of the inner layer and the outer layer. Lexue'er Company argues that the setting of the half-piece hollow cotton soft pad is to enhance the hand feel of holding the hot water bottle and does not have the function and effect of the insulation layer of the patent in dispute. This Court holds that the main principle of insulation is to weaken heat convection and heat conduction through physical isolation. The purpose of setting the insulation layer in the patent in dispute is to achieve the effects of insulation and burn prevention by controlling the heat convection of air between the inner and outer layers and blocking the heat conduction caused by physical contact between the inner and outer layers. The half-piece hollow cotton soft pad set in the accused infringing product is made of the same material as the insulation layer of the patent in dispute, is also structurally arranged between the inner layer and the outer layer, and although its size does not completely cover the inner layer and the outer layer, the manner of its arrangement effectively plays a role in weakening heat convection and heat conduction, and can also achieve the technical effects of insulation and burn prevention. Although the insulation and burn prevention effects of the half-piece hollow cotton may be slightly different from those of the whole-piece hollow cotton, a person of ordinary skill in the art, based on an understanding of the insulation principle, can determine that the difference is not substantial. Therefore, the "hollow cotton soft pad" and the "insulation layer" are equivalent. Furthermore, one of the distinguishing technical features of the utility model patent No. ZL200520015446.8 cited by Lexue'er Company for its prior art defense is the provision of an insulation layer between the inner layer and the outer layer. Lexue'er Company, on the one hand, asserts a prior art defense, and on the other hand, claims that the hollow cotton soft pad is not an insulation layer. This is logically self-contradictory. Moreover, as seen from the description of the above-mentioned utility model patent specification, the utility model patent consists of three layers, the inner layer being made of plastic and the outer layer being made of polyester cloth, so the hand feel is good, the insulation time is long, and the use effect is improved. It can be seen that the hand feel of a hot water bottle product is closely related to the material of its outer layer. Lexue'er Company's claim that the setting of the half-piece hollow cotton soft pad is only used to enhance hand feel lacks factual basis, and this Court does not support it.

In summary, the processing method of the accused infringing product is neither identical nor equivalent to the patented method in dispute and does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent in dispute.

III. Regarding the determination of damages for infringement in the original first-instance and second-instance judgments

Lexue'er Company argues that the second-instance judgment's determination of compensation for the use fee during the period of provisional protection exceeded Chen Shundi's claims. In this regard, this Court holds that Article 13 of the Patent Law provides: "After the publication of an application for a patent for invention, the applicant may require the entity or individual exploiting the invention to pay an appropriate fee." Therefore, the use fee during the period of provisional protection is an appropriate economic compensation payable to the patentee by the entity or individual exploiting the invention during the period from the publication of the invention patent application to the grant of the patent right. Its nature is different from the damages for infringement for exploiting the patent without the patentee's permission. Therefore, the patentee cannot claim the use fee during the period of provisional protection based on the cause of action for infringement damages but can only assert this fee separately. The cause of action in the lawsuit filed by Chen Shundi is a dispute over infringement of a patent for invention. During the first-instance trial, Chen Shundi claimed that the amount of damages for infringement included the use fee during the period of provisional protection. In this regard, the first-instance court informed him during the court hearing that this fee could not be claimed in this case and could be pursued in a separate lawsuit. It can be seen that the amount of compensation determined in the original first-instance judgment does not include the use fee during the period of provisional protection. The second-instance court, during the second-instance trial, determined that the amount of compensation decided by the first-instance court included the use fee during the period of provisional protection, which is indeed inappropriate. This Court hereby corrects this. Since the method used by Lexue'er Company to produce the accused infringing product does not infringe the patent in dispute and Lexue'er Company does not need to bear infringement liability, this Court will not further comment on its ground for retrial that the determination of the compensation amount in the original first-instance and second-instance judgments is manifestly unfair.

In summary, the method used by Lexue'er Company to produce the accused infringing product does not infringe the patent in dispute. The original first-instance and second-instance judgments applied the law improperly and the result of the judgments was erroneous and should be corrected. The main grounds for Lexue'er Company's application for retrial are established, and this Court supports them. In accordance with Article 11, paragraph 1, and Article 59, paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 207, paragraph 1, and Article 170, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2011) Liao Min San Zhong Zi No. 27 of the Liaoning High People's Court and the civil judgment (2010) Shen Zhong Min Si Chu Zi No. 389 of the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court are reversed;

2. All claims of Chen Shundi are dismissed.

The court acceptance fee for the first instance is RMB 18,300 and for the second instance is RMB 5,850, to be borne by Chen Shundi.

This judgment is final.
